messages:
john_doe (Customer): We're seeing a bunch of 5xx from the hosted API since ~09:12 UTC. Endpoint: POST /v1/generate. Error in response: "InternalError" and sometimes 502 gateway. Customer request_id examples: req_abcd1234, req_abcd1235. Repro steps: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -d '{"model":"gpt-xl","input":"hi"}'. Any idea? App is hitting timeouts and this is user-facing.

emily (Support): Thanks @john_doe — sorry about the outage. Can you paste one full response (headers + body) for req_abcd1234? Also which region/host (us-west1/us-east1)? We'll loop in SRE if we see 5xx patterns.

john_doe (Customer): Pasted below. Host: us-west1.

HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
Content-Type: application/json
x-request-id: req_abcd1234
x-upstream: gateway-01

{"error":"InternalError","message":"control_plane: routing policy timeout"}

emily (Support): Got it. @raj can you look? Looks like control-plane is returning 5xx (routing policy service or auth/session?). Customer reports repeated timeouts.

raj (SRE): On it. Pulling control-plane metrics. Quick check: recent spike in rpc.latency to routing-policy service ~09:08–09:20 UTC. Seeing a bunch of timeouts talking to config-db master replica. Correlation id from service logs: cid=9f3b0.

marta (Platform): We pushed a canary of the routing-policy change at 08:50 but it was small. Deploy bot?

deploy-bot: deploy d/routing-policy v2.3.1 succeeded on canary cluster at 2026-03-15T08:50:12Z :white_check_mark:

raj (SRE): Logs (truncated):

```
2026-03-15T09:09:03Z routing-policy ERROR cid=9f3b0 grpc: failed to call config-db: deadline exceeded
2026-03-15T09:09:04Z auth-proxy WARN session-check failed: config-db timeout
2026-03-15T09:09:06Z gateway ERROR upstream control_plane 502: routing-policy timeout
```

raj (SRE): Looks like config-db master had elevated GC pause plus a retry storm. Connection pool exhausted -> RPCs timeout -> routing-policy returns 5xx -> gateway surfaces 502/500 to customers. I'm going to open an incident and fail over config-db to replica.

emily (Support): ETA for mitigation?

raj (SRE): Failover in progress, promoting replica replica-03, increasing connection pool on routing-policy, and temporarily increasing RPC timeouts to 10s as a short-term mitigation.

marta (Platform): Rolling config tweak now to set routing policy cache TTL to 30s to reduce chatter while failover completes.

raj (SRE): Completed steps:
- promoted replica-03 as new master at 09:22 UTC
- routing-policy pool +50 connections
- rpc timeout bumped to 10s
- cache ttl 30s applied to routing-policy

Observability: error rate dropped to baseline by 09:28 UTC. No more 502s for affected requests.

emily (Support): Thanks @raj and @marta. @john_doe can you confirm if your app still sees 5xxs? If not, we'll mark this resolved and follow up with RCA.

john_doe (Customer): Confirmed — errors stopped around 09:28. Huge relief. Any recommended client-side mitigations? We saw our frontend retry loop thrash the API.

emily (Support): Recommend exponential backoff + jitter on retries, and abort after 3 attempts. Also using the 'try_fallback' header to route to a lower-cost fallback model during transient control-plane issues (we can enable per-customer if you want).

john_doe (Customer): Please enable fallback for our tenant id tnt_998 for the next 24h while you complete RCA.

marta (Platform): Done. Fallback header enabled for tenant tnt_998 at 09:40 UTC. Also creating a config DB alert to detect GC pause > 2s.

raj (SRE): I'll write up brief RCA: root cause was config-db GC pause on master during a routine compaction combined with retry storms from routing-policy. Mitigations: failover, increase pool, cache TTL, alerting. Long-term: investigate GC tuning and introduce slow-RPC circuit breaker on routing-policy.

emily (Support): Filing support ticket SUP-2026-1123 with incident notes and customer-sent logs. Closing thread once RCA doc is attached.

deploy-bot: incident SUP-2026-1123 created and linked to ops-incident-760

emily (Support): Thanks everyone. @john_doe we'll email you the incident summary and the steps to enable client-side fallback. Appreciate the fast confirmation.

john_doe (Customer): Thanks team, appreciate the quick turnaround :pray:
